section_1.title: Prerequisite: Defining the Planar Graph
section_1.content: Define a planar graph as a graph that can be drawn in a 2D plane without edges crossing. Introduce the elements: Vertices (V), Edges (E), and Faces (F).
section_1.example: Visualize a simple square with one diagonal (the K4 graph): 4 vertices, 6 edges, and the enclosed regions plus the infinite outer region (4 faces total).

section_2.title: Euler’s Characteristic Formula
section_2.content: Introduce the fundamental theorem: For any connected planar graph, V - E + F = 2. Explain how this constant relationship holds regardless of how the graph is stretched or distorted.
section_2.example: Using the K4 graph from section 1: V(4) - E(6) + F(4) = 2. Watch as the numbers animate and balance perfectly on screen.

section_3.title: The Concept of Duality
section_3.content: Explain the 'Dual Graph' construction: Place a point (vertex) inside every face of the original graph. Connect two new vertices if their corresponding faces share an edge. This creates a new, transformed graph.
section_3.example: Visualize a 'Spider-Web' graph. As we place dots in every gap, a new 'Ghost' graph emerges inside, highlighting how the structure mirrors the original.

section_4.title: The Duality Connection
section_4.content: Show the mathematical symmetry: The number of vertices in the dual (V') equals the number of faces in the original (F). The number of faces in the dual (F') equals the original vertices (V).
section_4.example: Use a color-coded animation: Vertices of the original graph turn into the faces of the dual, while faces of the original become the vertices of the dual.

section_5.title: Application: Network Resilience
section_5.content: Conclude by applying these concepts to real-world infrastructure. Duality helps engineers understand redundant paths in communication networks or circuit board layouts.
section_5.example: A city power grid map (the original graph). The dual graph reveals the 'weak points' in the grid architecture, allowing a technician to reinforce critical junctions.
